transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-08 15:00 PDT | Duration ~54m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Khatri (Redwood Product), Evan Morris (Saffron Head of ML), Laurel Singh (Infra Lead), Ravi Patel (CTO)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations for Saffron's conversational assistant. Ran three cost scenarios (low-latency, balanced, throughput-focused), discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, and agreed next steps for pilot benchmark and security docs.

Topics: Optimize console tour; automated batching suggestions; prefix vs KV cache tradeoffs; cost model assumptions; Dedicated sandbox run; security & compliance ask

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for carving time today. Uh quick intros? We'll go through the Optimize console, run a few scenarios for your traffic shape, and then map to a pilot.
[00:15] Evan Morris: Hey, Evan here. We're most curious about where we get wins without hurting 95th percentile latency.
[00:22] Diego Alvarez: Yeah, that's the common ask. Quick note, I'll pull up the console and the cost-sim so you can see how batching + cache behave across session lengths.
[00:35] Laurel Singh: For context, our assistant has a mix: 60% short queries (~20 tokens), 30% medium (50-150 tokens), 10% long sessions that use multi-turn memory; throughput target ~2k rps peak.
[00:50] Priya Khatri: Perfect, that traffic mix is what we used to seed the scenarios.
[00:55] [01:03] Diego Alvarez: (screen share) Ok opening Optimize -> Suggestions -> Batching & Cache. You'll see three recommended profiles we generated from your sample: low-latency, balanced-econ, and throughput-opt. The UI shows estimated per-1M-token cost and tail latency impact.
[01:25] Evan Morris: Already seeing numbers, nice. What is the baseline model here?
[01:30] Diego Alvarez: For the sim we used a 7B decoder model quantized to 4-bit, similar to what you mentioned in the intake form. Note the console label says "model proxy" which is Redwood's mapping to the version — occasionally the transcription shows that as "model proxie" in our logs.
[01:45] [01:50] Diego Alvarez: Balanced profile suggests modest batching (target batch size 6) + prefix KV cache for recent conversation turns. That reduces repeat compute on warm sessions and keeps P95 within your 250ms budget in the sim.
[02:05] Evan Morris: Wait — prefix cache vs KV cache — is that the same thing? I'm still fuzzy on terminology.
[02:12] Maya Chen: Good question. We often use "prefix cache" to mean caching entire token prefixes for sessions so subsequent responses reuse autoregressive context; "KV cache" tends to be the runtime key/value activation snapshot. In practice both help but in different ways — prefix cache yields bigger algorithmic savings for repeated prompts, KV cache is lower-level and used by the runtime for attention states. Sometimes transcription will say "K V" with spaces.
[02:38] Ravi Patel: If we use prefix cache aggressively, do we risk stale context for multi-turns?
[02:43] Diego Alvarez: That's a fair tradeoff. Prefix cache works best when user turns are highly repetitive or you have canonical system prompts. If you need strict recency, we suggest targeted cache TTLs or selective caching for non-sensitive prefixes. The console lets you configure TTL by route.
[03:05] [03:10] Laurel Singh: What about batching? Our burstiness spikes... We care about latency at the 95th. How do you keep batching from hurting single-user latency?
[03:20] Diego Alvarez: Two levers: max-latency SLO per request (we'll cap micro-batching delay) and adaptive batching by request size. So for small short queries we can still aggregate but with a strict micro-delay cap — e.g., 10ms wait or until batch size hit. For your balanced scenario we set micro-delay 8–12ms which buys 20–30% token savings while keeping P95 under target in our sim.
[03:50] Evan Morris: The cost sim shows a 38% reduction in token compute for balanced — what assumptions are baked in?
[03:58] Priya Khatri: The sim assumes KV caching hit rate of 28% in balanced, 12% in low-latency (we keep caching conservative), and 45% in throughput-opt. Also assumes batching efficiency curve derived from your average sequence length distribution. We include vagaries like kernel selection overhead and amortized startup for GPUs.
[04:25] [04:30] Diego Alvarez: Also important: Dedicated vs Hosted. If you go Dedicated, you get reserved throughput and better predictable latency at the cost of commit. Our sim shows Dedicated reduces per-token tail latency by about 15% at high utilization because of warm kernels and pinned memory, but your unit cost calculation needs commit amortization.
[04:50] Ravi Patel: Could you show a scenario where Dedicated is better financially?
[04:55] Diego Alvarez: Sure. I'll flip to the "commit amortization" sheet in the cost-sim. For steady-state 1.5M tokens/day with 70% GPU utilization, Dedicated with moderate commit breaks even at roughly 8 months vs hosted for your model family. For spiky seasonal loads hosted can be cheaper short-term.
[05:20] [05:30] Evan Morris: What about quantization regressions? We're cautious about quality changes with 4-bit.
[05:35] Maya Chen: We recommend a canary eval suite — Redwood Optimize integrates with your evals. You can pin a percentage of traffic to a quantized variant and monitor quality deltas. We can help set up the canary.
[05:50] [06:05] Laurel Singh: Security question: if we use Private deployment, does prefix cache live in our VPC?
[06:12] Priya Khatri: Yes, in Private deployments the cache state and KV storage reside in customer-managed infrastructure; keys and artifacts stay in the VPC. We do offer KMS/HSM integrations for keys.
[06:25] Ravi Patel: Ok good.
[06:30] [06:40] Diego Alvarez: Back to the console: here's a heatmap of session lengths (yours) and the predicted cache hit rate curve. See how long sessions create opportunities for >60% savings with selective prefix caching?
[06:55] Evan Morris: Hmm interesting. Does that cause more memory pressure?
[07:00] Diego Alvarez: Yes if you cache full prefixes for many concurrent long sessions you need more memory; that's why Optimize suggests TTL tiering and active eviction policies — we model that into cost so you see memory footprint vs token savings tradeoffs.
[07:18] [07:40] Maya Chen: Quick demo: I'll toggle to the "Autosuggest" tab — this will propose batching/concurrency params plus a recommended cache profile for each route. You can accept or tweak, then run a simulated traffic sweep.
[07:55] [08:05] Diego Alvarez: Running a sim now — this is the 2k-rps spike test. Balanced profile keeps P95 at ~240ms, cost down 34%. Throughput-opt lowers cost an extra 12% but pushes P95 to ~320ms. Low-latency keeps P95 ~180ms but cost is higher, fewer batching gains.
[08:35] Evan Morris: Those numbers match our internal threshold around 300ms. For customer-facing flows we want <250ms.
[08:42] Diego Alvarez: So likely balanced profile is the starting point. For background or non-customer routes you can enable throughput-opt.
[08:50] [09:05] Evan Morris: Can we mix per-route policies? e.g., low-latency for checkout flows, balanced for discovery?
[09:12] Priya Khatri: Absolutely, Optimize is route-aware and suggestions are per-route. You can also pin versions per route.
[09:20] [09:40] Laurel Singh: Any gotchas on prefix caching for PII-sensitive prompts?
[09:45] Maya Chen: We recommend not caching prompts that contain PII or subject to retention policies. The console allows regex filters and route-level opt-outs. For Private deployments those caches live in your infra; for Hosted we can redact or avoid caching based on rules.
[10:05] [10:20] Diego Alvarez: A quick aside — we sometimes see customers expect prefetched KV cache to always hit; in reality hit rate depends on session locality and user behavior. The sim gives you a range (p10/p90) to calibrate expectations.
[10:40] Evan Morris: Let's talk about metrics we'll monitor during a pilot.
[10:45] Maya Chen: Core metrics: per-route P95 latency, tokens per request, KV hit rate, batch size distribution, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll ship a dashboard template that maps to these.
[11:00] [11:15] Diego Alvarez: Also important: an early smoke test to validate quality. We'll run evals on the canary traffic and check key prompts.
[11:25] Ravi Patel: For the pilot, what's the minimal dataset you need from us?
[11:30] Priya Khatri: Sample traffic histogram, a few representative prompts (10-20) for quality checks, and an indication of the routes you consider critical. Laurel mentioned you'll share the traffic profile.
[11:45] Laurel Singh: Yes I'll send that by end of day tomorrow.
[11:50] [12:05] Diego Alvarez: Ok next I'll show the cost-sim export. (shared link) https://redwood.app/sims/ffx-57821 — this has scenario tabs and the export CSV.
[12:20] Evan Morris: Great. Could you annotate the assumptions in the CSV?
[12:25] Maya Chen: We'll add an assumptions column.
[12:30] [12:45] Diego Alvarez: Tying to commit calculus — if you want Dedicated, we'll size the GPU pool to meet your 2k rps at target P95. The console's capacity estimator will propose node types and commit tiers. Note: commit discounts show up in the same sim sheet.
[12:58] Evan Morris: One more question — how durable is the prefix cache across restarts? If a pod restarts do we lose it?
[13:05] Diego Alvarez: Good question. By default runtime keeps cache in memory for speed; for longer-term durability we can back it to a local SSD-backed store or customer object store in Private. There's a tradeoff between faster in-memory hits and durability. We'll recommend per-route settings.
[13:25] [13:45] Priya Khatri: Security/process — Redwood provides audit logs per token-level access?
[13:50] Maya Chen: We provide detailed audit trails for model invocations, route changes, and who approved config changes. For Private deployments logs stay in your S3/KV. We can also forward to SIEM.
[14:05] [14:20] Evan Morris: Sounds good.
[14:25] Diego Alvarez: Wrapping up, the recommended pilot: 2-week Dedicated sandbox with balanced profile, run 1k–2k synthetic spike tests, and sample canary traffic at 10% production. We'll measure P95 and cost delta.
[14:45] [14:55] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: I'll send the cost-sim + console recording; Diego will provision the sandbox and run the benchmark; Priya will send SOC2 and Private deployment checklist. Laurel to share the traffic histogram.
[15:10] Ravi Patel: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. We'll review the cost-sim and pick dates to run the pilot.
[15:18] Evan Morris: Quick note — can you also include a short note comparing our current infra spend to projected Redwood spend? Even a ballpark.
[15:25] Maya Chen: Yes will include a delta sheet in the CSV.
[15:30] [15:40] Diego Alvarez: Ok we'll follow up in email with links and a proposed pilot start date.
[15:45] (end)

Meeting recap (auto): Balanced profile recommended as starter; prefix+KV caching plus micro-batching yields biggest wins for long sessions; Dedicated helpful for predictable latency at scale; pilot agreed.

Resources shared during call: https://redwood.app/sims/ffx-57821 (cost-sim export), Optimize console recording link (will be sent), SOC2 summary (will be shared).

Explicit next steps: Maya to send cost-sim CSV and recording; Diego to provision sandbox and run benchmark; Laurel to send traffic histogram.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels in product names ("Redwood Dedicate") and KV spelled as separate letters in transcript.
